newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan eyes JR East shares sale after April - paper.
newsitem.headline: Japan eyes JR East shares sale after April - paper.

text.p: JNR Settlement Corp is looking into another listing of state-owned shares in East Japan Railway Co (JR East) after April, Yasuo Nishimura, president of the state-owned agent, was quoted as saying on Thursday.

Nishimura told reporters that his company will consider another sale of JR East shares after the stock market has settled down following the end-March corporate book closings in Japan. His comments were published by the financial daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun.
The state-owned agent in charge of settling the debt and assets left by the Japanese National Railways (JNR), still holds 1.5 million JR East shares after having listed 2.5 million shares in 1993.
When the heavily indebted JNR was split into seven Japan Railway (JR) group companies in April 1987, the government inherited two-thirds of JNR's debt, or 25.5 trillion yen.
The government had hoped to slash the debt by selling land left by JNR and listing state-owned shares of JR firms, but this has been delayed while interest payments have grown.
East JR and West Japan Railway Co (JR West), the two biggest, are the only members of the seven-company JR group which are listed.
